subject: Handback & escrow: proof-of-delete and attestation options for private VPC storage
messages:

Subject: Handback & Escrow: Proof of Delete for Private VPC Storage

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — Acme is finalizing controls for our private VPC deployment and security has a few specific asks we need to document before procurement:

1) Can Redwood provide cryptographic proof-of-delete (e.g., hash-based tombstone + signed attestations) for customer-managed storage when a tenant requests a wipe?
2) What is the end-to-end timeline from API-initiated wipe to verifiable physical purge for object stores and snapshot backups?
3) Do you support escrowed snapshots (export) and can those be placed in a customer-managed vault for handback?
4) Is there a third-party attestation option (signed by an auditor) that Redwood can provide for a one-time handback event?
5) How do you handle KMS keys for customer-controlled keys (bring-your-own-key) vs Redwood-managed keys during a handback?

We attached our RFI (Acme_Security_RFI_v2.pdf) with desired evidence types. Would appreciate a short answer + proposed next steps/call availability.

Best,
Nora

security@acme-health.com

Subject: Re: Handback & Escrow: Proof of Delete for Private VPC Storage

Hi Nora — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise mapping to each ask plus recommended evidence packages and next steps. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through and align on SLA language.

Summary answers (high level):
• Proof-of-delete: Yes — for customer-controlled storage we offer a multi-part evidence package: API-triggered wipe log, final object hash index, internal purge job execution logs, and a signed erase certificate (CSV) that includes the pre- and post-delete hash digests. For hosted snapshots we can also produce a snapshot manifest and hash list. The signed certificate uses Redwood's deployment signing key; we can also route through a neutral auditor for a third-party signature on request.

• Timeline: Typical path for object stores: API wipe -> tombstone mark (near real-time) -> async purge job within retention window -> permanent removal from live store + deletion from snapshot/backup chain within 5–15 business days depending on snapshot cadence. For faster purges we can execute an expedited purge process (physical overwrite/compaction) with an agreed SLA (typically 3–7 business days) and elevated privilege review.

• Escrowed snapshots: Supported. We can export encrypted snapshot bundles to a customer-managed bucket (S3/GCS) or to an escrow provider. Export manifests contain checksums and a signed provenance file.

• Third-party attestation: Supported as an engagement — we can coordinate with our compliance partner (SOC2 auditor) to provide an attestation letter for a one-time handback. This requires 10 business days lead time and a scoped statement-of-work.

• KMS keys: For BYOK (customer-managed keys) the encryption keys remain under the customer's KMS/HSM; Redwood never persists plaintext. In handback scenarios the customer retains the keys; we produce manifests encrypted with the customer key. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate and retire keys per the handback SOW; key deletion and wrap/unwrap logs are included in the evidence package.

Recommended evidence packages (examples):
1) Standard evidence bundle (no third-party): API activity log, object hash index, purge job logs, erase_certificate.csv (signed), snapshot_manifest.json (if applicable). Delivery within 10 business days after request.
2) Expedited purge + escrow: expedited purge runbook, export bundle to customer bucket, signed manifest, and on-demand purge confirmation. SLA: 3–7 business days; additional fee applies.
3) Auditor-attested handback: Coordinate SOW with auditor, Redwood provides all artifacts + auditor issues attestation. Lead time: ~10 business days.

Next steps / proposals:
• I attached a short playbook (redwood-handback-playbook.pdf) and a sample erase certificate (sample-erase-cert.csv) for your security team to review.
• If you want a third-party attestation, we can draft a SOW and budget estimate — Karthik, can you draft a scope and ballpark?
• If Acme prefers BYOK, we can schedule an operations run to validate key policies prior to go-live.

Would 11:00 PT tomorrow for a 30-min call work?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks, that helps. A couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule:

1) For the erase_certificate.csv: will that include the object-level SHA256 before/after digests and a Redwood signature block? We need line-level artifacts for our change control.
2) For BYOK: can Redwood accept a customer HSM key (PKCS#11) for encryption of snapshot exports so that Redwood never has the wrap key?
3) For expedited purge: can you describe exactly which API call(s) an engineer would invoke to initiate an expedited purge and what RBAC is required? We need this to write our automation runbooks.
4) Third-party attestation: can you confirm cost ranges for past engagements (ballpark)? That will help me with procurement.

If possible include short examples (API path + sample payload) in your reply.

Best,
Nora
